question: Why do atoms and non-polar molecules have no dipole moment?

options.text: Because their electronic charge cloud is asymmetrically distributed
Because their electronic charge cloud is missing
Because their electronic charge cloud is symmetrically distributed
Because their electronic charge cloud is scattered

solution:
The correct answer is **__Because their Electronic Charge Cloud is symmetrically Distributed__****__.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Atom and Non-Polar molecules have no dipole moment **because their Electronic Charge cloud is symmetrically distributed.**
 
• Nonpolar bonds occur because there is the difference in electronegativity between two atoms is less than 0.4.
 
• **Non-polar bonds do not have any type of net dipole moment** and are generally formed in compounds where there is a presence of symmetry. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In chemistry, a dipole refers to **the separation of charges within a molecule between two covalently bonded types of atoms or atoms that share an ionic bond**.
 
• The main difference between polar and dipolar molecules is **polar molecules have two opposite ends with opposite electrical charges, whereas dipolar molecules have only two poles**.
